definition: A buffering hint tells Firehose how much data or time to accumulate before destination delivery.
A delivery role grants Firehose the permissions it needs to read sources, process records, and write destinations.
A trust policy specifies who can assume an IAM role.
COPY is the Redshift command Firehose uses to load staged S3 objects into a table.
A schema describes the field names and types used to interpret input records.
A deserializer reads encoded input data into the fields used by format conversion.
A serializer writes interpreted data into the chosen output format.
A columnar format stores data by column to reduce storage and query work.
Deaggregation separates multiple combined input records before further processing.
Dynamic partitioning uses record values to send data to selected S3 prefixes.
Base64 is the text encoding required for record data returned by a Firehose Lambda transformation.
Backfill loads data that an earlier delivery attempt skipped.
A manifest identifies the S3 objects skipped during a Redshift load so they can be loaded manually.
At-least-once delivery allows a record to be delivered again when an attempt is retried.
Direct PUT sends application records to Firehose through its PutRecord or PutRecordBatch APIs.
Parquet is a columnar file format that Firehose can produce from JSON before S3 delivery.
ORC is a columnar file format that Firehose can produce from JSON before S3 delivery.
